<action type="say">
Got it—Philly 19103, one dedicated office circuit, flexible next month in the afternoon, and you want to stay well under ~$800.

I can’t see specific local businesses directly from here, but I can guide you to get something more like $300–$600 instead of $800+ and avoid getting ripped off. Here’s how I’d play it:

1) What you should ask for (to keep scope tight)
- Tell them: “I need one new 20A 120V dedicated circuit for a small office (computers/monitors), in EMT/NM as appropriate, with a new breaker in the existing panel and 1–2 duplex outlets.”
- Confirm: panel has space for a new breaker, run is roughly X feet (even a rough guess helps), and no crazy fishing through finished ceilings if you can avoid it.
- Say clearly: “Please quote labor + materials, including permit if required.”

2) Target price range (Philly, non‑emergency, small job)
- Reasonable ballpark: usually around $350–$650 total depending on:
  - Distance from panel to outlet
  - How hard it is to fish cable (finished walls vs open basement/ceiling)
  - Whether a permit is pulled and city fees
If someone is quoting $900+ for a simple, short run with easy access, I’d treat that as “only if I have no other options.”

3) How to search and filter (to avoid high-end pricing)
On HomeAdvisor/Angi/Thumbtack/Google Maps:
- Search: “licensed electrician 19103” or “residential electrician circuit installation”
- Filters:
  - Rating 4.5+ with at least ~20 reviews
  - No “24/7 emergency only” shops (they tend to be pricey)
- In descriptions, look for: “small jobs welcome”, “residential specialist”, or “panel/circuit upgrades.”

4) Script to message 3–5 electricians for quotes
Copy/paste and tweak this in apps/email/text:

“Hi, I’m in 19103. I need ONE new 20A dedicated 120V circuit run from my existing panel to a small home office for computers/monitor. Flexible on timing (any weekday afternoon next month is fine).  
The run is approximately [X feet, e.g. ‘30–40 ft’], mostly through [unfinished basement / finished walls].  
Can you give a ballpark estimate (labor + materials, including permit if needed) and your soonest afternoon availability next month? I’m not in a rush, just looking for a solid job at a reasonable price.”

Ask each:
- “Typical total range for this: low–high?”
- “Any extra fee for coming to look first?”
- “Is the quote flat-rate or time + materials?”

5) How to pick the best value
Lean toward the one that:
- Is licensed and insured, and will pull a permit if required.
- Gives a clear range, e.g. “$450–$600 depending on actual run length,” instead of super vague.
- Has solid reviews mentioning “fair price,” “didn’t oversell,” “small job.”

If you want, tell me:
- Rough distance from the panel to where you want the outlet (short/medium/long or feet estimate)
- Whether the path is mostly open (unfinished basement/ceiling) or finished walls

I’ll help you tighten the description and I can draft 2–3 tailored messages you can send to specific listings you find, plus help you evaluate any quotes you get so you don’t end up paying $800+ for a simple run. </action>
